gaps.category: Pesticide and fertiliser dealers (cat 14 not_reached): fertiliser licence and hazardous-substances dealer duties
gaps.first_search: พ.ร.บ.ปุ๋ย พ.ศ. 2518 ผู้ขายปุ๋ย ใบอนุญาต บัญชีรับจ่าย รายงาน กรมวิชาการเกษตร
gaps.why: Thailand has very many small farm-input shops. K08 covers only the pesticide register. The Fertiliser Act (พ.ร.บ.ปุ๋ย) licences sellers and requires sales and stock records, and nobody checked it. I am unsure of the exact record duty.

gaps.category: Small food producers and community enterprises: Thai FDA licences, GMP and OTOP/community-enterprise registration
gaps.first_search: วิสาหกิจชุมชน รายงานประจำปี กรมส่งเสริมการเกษตร ทะเบียน ผู้ประกอบการ OTOP อย. สถานที่ผลิตอาหาร ต่ออายุ
gaps.why: Thailand has a huge base of home and community food producers (OTOP, วิสาหกิจชุมชน). They face FDA notification, label and GMP duties and annual community-enterprise reporting to CPD. K16 only killed the factory licence renewal. Cat 20 searched small food producers only as a one-line mention.

gaps.category: Value-added tax and small-business tax duties: VAT registration threshold (1.8m baht), e-filing, withholding tax (ภ.ง.ด.3/53) and the e-Withholding Tax system
gaps.first_search: ภ.ง.ด.3 ภ.พ.30 ผู้ประกอบการรายย่อย ยื่นแบบ ออนไลน์ หัก ณ ที่จ่าย อิเล็กทรอนิกส์ กรมสรรพากร 2569
gaps.why: The pass covered no Revenue Department recurring duty (only K15 e-Tax invoice). Monthly withholding-tax and VAT filings fall on a very large number of sole traders and family firms. The pass excluded generic accounting software, but a niche vertical (for example, filing for households that rent out rooms) might not be excluded. Unsure whether this is in scope.

gaps.category: Drone, radio and telecom-equipment licences, and the 2024-26 drone registration rules
gaps.first_search: โดรนเกษตร ขึ้นทะเบียน กสทช. กพท. ใบอนุญาตนักบิน พ่นสารเคมี ผู้ประกอบการ 2568
gaps.why: The new CAAT and NBTC drone registration and insurance rules hit many small agricultural-spraying drone operators. Agricultural drone services boomed in Thai farming, with registration, pilot licences and pesticide-spraying permits. This is a sector with many small operators and a 2024-26 rule change.

gaps.category: Fishing vessels and small-scale fisheries: IUU crew registration, vessel licences, PIPO port-in/port-out and fishing logbooks
gaps.first_search: เรือประมงพาณิชย์ ใบอนุญาตใช้เรือ ต่ออายุ สมุดบันทึกการจับสัตว์น้ำ ลูกเรือ ขึ้นทะเบียน กรมประมง พ.ร.ก.การประมง 2558
gaps.why: Thai fishing is a major sector with many small family boat owners under the Royal Ordinance on Fisheries 2015. K18 only covers catch certificates for exporters. Vessel licence renewal, crew contracts, VMS and logbooks are recurring duties for small boat owners. Cat 30 searched fish only under export traceability.

gaps.category: Cross-border trade duties on small operators: border-trade traders, import/export licences for restricted goods, and the 2025-26 rules on cheap Chinese imports (VAT on low-value parcels, e-commerce seller registration, TISI product-standard marks)
gaps.first_search: ผู้ขายออนไลน์ จดทะเบียนพาณิชย์อิเล็กทรอนิกส์ DBD มอก. บังคับ สินค้านำเข้า ภาษีมูลค่าเพิ่ม พัสดุ 2569 ผู้ประกอบการรายย่อย
gaps.why: The pass covers no importer-side duties apart from the EU-bound K05 and K06. The 2024-25 changes (VAT on imports under 1,500 baht, the TISI mandatory standard drive against online sellers, e-commerce operator registration with DBD) affect thousands of small online sellers and importers. The pass did not search this.

candidates.buyer: Small licensed foreign-banknote exchange shops (non-bank 'Authorised Persons') and prospective new entrants
candidates.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
candidates.evidence: https://www.bot.or.th/th/laws-and-rules/public-hearing/public-hearing-20260921-money-changer.html ; https://www.bot.or.th/content/dam/bot/public-hearing/fx-regulation-nov-2025/public-hearing-20260819-money%20changer.pdf (PDF text read locally: BOT 'plans to significantly revise qualifications, criteria and licence format ... capital, branch management, system standards and service limits'); https://www.thaipbs.or.th/news/content/260182
candidates.existing: Competitor search in Thai (โปรแกรมแลกเงิน / POS ซื้อขายธนบัตรต่างประเทศ) found no Thai money-changer product, only foreign tools (CurrencyXchanger, FX-Star on G2/Capterra) and Tanzanian/Pakistani systems. Bank-run exchange kiosks (KBank) are a different segment.
candidates.known_note: Different buyer group (licensed money changers, not gold shops) and a different authority (BOT, not AMLO).
candidates.name: Money-changer (บุคคลรับอนุญาต) Licence-Upgrade and Monthly Reporting Desk
candidates.trigger: BOT draft criteria on public hearing 21 Sep-20 Oct 2026 (earlier hearing 19 Aug-18 Sep 2026). Applicants for 2027 must file in December 2026; BOT pauses new applications in 2027 and reopens in 2028 (maybe 2 rounds a year). All existing licensees must upgrade in 2027 under new rules (registered capital, branch count, systems standards, per-customer limits) and file results for BOT case-by-case review. Existing duties: monthly volume report to BOT and a report to AMLO above THB 2m per customer (Thai PBS, unverified against the current notice).
candidates.unchecked: Number of current licensees (2017 figure of about 1,943 is old); the exact new system standard and per-customer limits in the full draft; the BOT monthly report format and AMLO duty; whether foreign vendors or Thai POS vendors already sell a compliant system; shop owners' willingness to pay. Full PDF text was read only in its first section.

A draft ministerial regulation on new standards for about 1,000 centres is reported (date and status unknown).

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K07. Employer must notify DOE of migrant worker start/end within 15 days (7 days for MOU workers), fine up to THB 20,000 (mgronline 9620000038882 via search, unverified in full). 90-day report is the worker's duty to Immigration. No household-employer-specific DOE system found. Live-in carers for elderly are covered by the care-home candidate below (caregiver registration with DHSS, 420-hour course).

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K09. Controlling Auctions and Second-hand Trade Act B.E. 2474: Thairath/Thansettakij (Feb 2025) report House industry committee reviewing amendments, fine for not recording sellers is only THB 2,000, draft would widen 'second-hand trade' to electronic means. Status of bill after Feb 2025 not confirmed. Dealers also need a local public-health licence (hazardous-to-health business). data.go.th has a list of licensed dealers (dataset_40_204), so a lead list exists.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Second-hand side is K09. Pawnshops: LH Bank outlook says about 1.41m pledgors and THB 29.4bn of pledges in FY2025, over 90% gold. Could not find the pawn licence regime, record-keeping format or any AMLO reporting duty; unverified. Logged as a weak, unchecked candidate.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Related to K10 (no new rejection). New evidence: BOT/AMLO joint tightening 30 Dec 2025; Foreign Exchange Controller Notice No. 36 (gazetted 26 Jan 2026) makes only large gold traders (domestic gold turnover over THB 10bn/yr, 5-yr average) report transactions, so small shops are outside it; BOT hearing 22 Jul-20 Aug 2026 on cash/payment-source rules for gold-bar sales at gold shops, with a THB 10m cash ceiling floated (title only). Competitor search for gold-shop POS found no named Thai product.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler licence or register found. DIW says only 2 integrated end-of-life vehicle plants exist (Chonburi, Ayutthaya) (Bangkokbiznews 28 Jun 2026). Crime news on chop shops with 100+ registration books. Nothing recorded as a candidate.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Animal Epidemics Act B.E. 2558 movement permits are issued through DLD's e-movement system, so a state tool already covers it. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Slaughter Control for Meat Distribution Act B.E. 2559; three ministerial regulations in force 25 Nov 2021. Slaughterers must notify animal count, source, date and time (fines per head, e.g. up to THB 20,000 per pig). DLD inspects licensed slaughterhouses twice a year; 364 licences cancelled, 51 suspended. Whether pork-stall (เขียงหมู) cutters need a licence is unclear. Weak, unverified candidate.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Nothing mandatory found. TAS 8207-2567 (GAP for bee farms) is voluntary; research shows record-keeping weak. DOAE Chiang Mai tests honey free. No registry or recurring duty.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Search returned only generic DLD news; no veterinary-drug sales register, form or 2025-26 rule found. Unverified, not rejected. The statutes are the Veterinary Drug Act and Veterinary Profession Act; numbers and forms not checked.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Groundwater Act licences (drilling, use, discharge) from DGR; water-use fees by purpose. No reporting format or fee-collection data found. Weak, unverified.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Bangkok crackdown on unlicensed septic-truck operators in Ratchathewi (June 2026). Cabinet approved a draft ministerial regulation on fees for sanitation-waste licences in 2025 (gazette status unknown). Some municipal ordinances (e.g. Tak Fa) require transport documents. No national manifest system found. K02 covers industrial waste, not this buyer group.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K04. Building Control Act s.32 bis annual inspection of controlled buildings; lift owners hire engineers; boiler internal inspections every 1-5 years under DIW. Many commercial inspection vendors already exist. Buyers are building owners and juristic persons, not quiet small firms.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: DOH survey 2025: only 9.5% of village waterworks pass the potable-water criteria; April 2026 DOH-NANOTEC MOU for test kits and surveillance. No licence regime for village waterworks found. Operators are village committees and local governments with weak payment ability. Weak, unverified.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: No search spent: K08 already covers the pesticide-shop register and the budget went to categories with no prior idea. Fertiliser dealers not checked.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K07. DOE inspected 43,832 workplaces and prosecuted 1,442 from Oct 2024 to 13 May 2025. MOU intake deadlines in 2025. Recruiter licence regime and any periodic report not found; unverified.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Cemeteries and Crematoria Act B.E. 2528: local officer issues a 3-year licence. Sept 2026 Chachoengsao case (licence not renewed, order to remove the cemetery; Thai PBS and Naewna). No funeral-business law found. No software angle. Weak.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: CICOT Halal Affairs Notice 5/2569 on extending halal certification; 2025 rules lengthened the mark period from 1 year to 2-3 years. Foundation/association annual-report duties and online system not confirmed. Weak.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Government required all app-based ride drivers to hold a public driving licence by 30 Sep 2026 (deadline just passed, no extension seen). Public motorcycle taxis may inspect at any private inspection centre one month ahead (Sept 2026). DLT cracking down on expired taxis (Mar 2026). A document-expiry reminder tool is possible but thin. K19 truck GPS already rejected.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers: strong lead (see candidate). Street vendors: BMA vendor rules revised 2024 draft; no recurring licence filing or software gap found.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Elder-care centres (strong, see candidate) and spa/massage under the Health Business Act 2559 (weak). Driving schools: only open-data list and nothing on a reporting system. Nurseries: authority unclear (conflicting sources between social development office and local government); nothing new. Tattoo studios and hunting outfitters: not applicable, no licensing regime found. Small food producers: K16.

Corn buyers of 50 t or more must notify volume, storage place and price and keep a stock-control ledger, per Matichon and Naewna news of unknown date. DIT inspects buying points. coverage.found: 1 search. The 10-year clinic licence renewal wave (325 Bangkok clinics licensed in 2015) and SSO claim steps were not found. Paying the fee counts as renewal under a 2021 decree (old news). Claims side is covered by K13 (A-MED Care). Candidate 12 (weak). Labs: no separate search.

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: 1 search. Pharmacy registers are covered by K12. Hazardous Substances Act licences are being moved online per a cabinet decision (date unverified). The search found no Thai precursor-chemical rule for chemical shops. Candidate 17 (weak, related to K08).

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: 2 searches (construction labour; quarries). Construction: only migrant-labour raids (121 undocumented workers found at a Rayong site, June 2026), and the ministerial regulation on abandonment of government works (27 Jul 2026), which concerns public procurement. Quarries and explosives licences: the search returned nothing useful (not_reached in substance). Related to candidate 1.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
